archimate:Goal.name: Health Sector Monitoring and Auditing: Ensure accountable use of health funds through auditability, oversight reporting and appropriate public disclosure
archimate:Goal.documentation:
An advanced application service layer achieved by establishing continuous, end-to-end transparency, automated compliance verification, and public accountability mechanisms across the entire health expenditure lifecycle. This oversight framework integrates internal financial controls with external reporting portals, allowing oversight bodies, independent auditors, and the public to track the flow of health funding from national allocation down to frontline service delivery.
Its primary purpose is to safeguard public resources, eliminate corruption, and build institutional trust within the healthcare system. By ensuring that every transaction leaves an indelible, auditable digital footprint, it detects fiscal irregularities in real time, simplifies complex statutory auditing, and fulfills democratic mandates for open government through accessible public disclosures.
Example: A national health insurance authority implements a unified monitoring and auditing service; the system automatically flags overlapping or unusually high medical claims for internal review, generates standardized, machine-readable financial reports for the supreme audit institution, and updates a public-facing digital dashboard showing exactly how much emergency pandemic funding was distributed to and spent by each municipal hospital.
